analysis.title: Gap Inc. (GAP): F3Q26 Earnings Review: Old Navy shows sequential progress but softer start to holiday drives reduced FY26 outlook
key_insights: GAP reported F3Q26 adjusted EPS of $0.82 (reported, adjusted), above GS consensus of $0.77 and FactSet consensus of $0.78, and lowered FY26 guidance.
Consolidated comps were flat Y/Y, in line with GS and below consensus of +1.4%. Net sales rose 2% Y/Y vs GS/consensus of +1.9%/+1.8%.

By brand, comps were Gap +9% (vs GS/consensus +11.0%/+9.3%), Old Navy flat (vs -4% in F2Q, GS/consensus -0.5%), Banana Republic -3% (vs GS/consensus +3.0%/+1.8%) and Athleta -15% (vs GS/consensus -10.0%/-11%).

Adjusted gross margin of 42.4% missed GS/consensus of 42.9%/43.0%. SG&A leveraged about 130bps Y/Y, mainly on lower incentive compensation, so adjusted operating margin of 9.8% beat GS/consensus of 9.3%/9.4%.
Underlying merchandise margin rose 10bps excluding about 60bps of tariff benefit and about 30bps of fuel pressure.

Management said Old Navy tracked ahead of expectations through September. Warm weather then pressured seasonal demand in October and early November. Trends recovered to roughly the F3Q rate as temperatures normalized, but only recently.
FY26 adjusted EPS guidance was cut to $2.29-$2.34 from $2.35-$2.45, vs GS/FactSet consensus of $2.42/$2.39. Net sales growth is now roughly flat Y/Y, from +1.0%-1.5% prior.

FY26 adjusted gross margin is now guided down slightly Y/Y (was up slightly) and adjusted operating margin to about 7.2% (from about 7.4%-7.6%), despite about $46mn of incremental tariff benefit (about 30bps).
Adjusted SG&A is now expected to leverage slightly (was about flat), reflecting about $150mn of cost savings and lower incentive compensation.
F4Q guidance: net sales down 1% to flat vs GS/consensus +3.4%/+3.1%, gross margin 38.0%-38.3% vs 39.5%/39.2%, implied adjusted EPS $0.56-$0.61 vs GS/FactSet consensus $0.74/$0.71.
The F4Q Old Navy comp guide of -1% to -2% includes the early-November pressure and roughly flat recent trends. A stronger pent-up seasonal demand response is upside not in guidance.
Athleta appointed Ashley Kechter as Brand President and CEO effective December 14, and the company is conducting a comprehensive review of the brand.
GS calls the result soft against low investor expectations. It sees Old Navy as a show-me story and Athleta as a significant offset to upside, and remains constructive.
GS cut FY26/FY27/FY28 EPS estimates to $2.33/$2.45/$2.74 from $2.42/$2.69/$3.00 and lowered its 12-month price target to $25 from $27 (Buy rating).

market_movers.rationale: Price target cut to $25 from $27 as GS rolls forward its Q5-Q8 EV/EBITDA method and lowers the target multiple to 4.00x from 4.35x on weaker growth and margin recovery. Buy rating kept with 33.0% upside from $18.79.

earnings_insights: F3Q26 adjusted EPS reported $0.82 (adjusted, reported 11/19) vs GS consensus $0.77 and FactSet consensus $0.78. GAAP EPS was $0.86, including $0.04 of one-time items.
F3Q26 adjusted gross margin 42.4% reported vs GS est 42.9% and consensus 43.0%. Adjusted operating margin 9.8% reported vs GS est 9.3% and consensus 9.4%.
F3Q26 net sales $4,011mn reported vs GS est $4,016mn, up 2% Y/Y. Inventory was down 6.3% Y/Y.
FY26 adjusted EPS guidance $2.29-$2.34 (company guide, cut from $2.35-$2.45) vs GS/FactSet consensus $2.42/$2.39.
F4Q26 adjusted EPS implied by company guidance at $0.56-$0.61 vs GS/FactSet consensus $0.74/$0.71.
GS estimates: FY26 EPS $2.33 (from $2.42), FY27 $2.45 (from $2.69), FY28 $2.74 (from $3.00). Quarterly EPS: Jan-27 quarter $0.61, Apr-27 $0.44, Jul-27 $0.59.
risk_factors: Long-term cost headwinds from freight and wage inflation driving margin pressure.
Prolonged pressure on the low-income consumer's spending power.
Increased competition with off-price peers or other apparel businesses.
Athleta remains challenged, with new leadership starting in December and a likely longer path to recovery.
Weather-driven seasonal demand swings at Old Navy, as seen in October and early November.

tension_points.bull_case: Old Navy improved sequentially to flat comps in F3Q from -4% in F2Q, trends recently recovered to roughly the F3Q rate, and pent-up seasonal demand is potential upside not embedded in the F4Q guide. The Gap brand also remains healthy at +9%.
tension_points.bear_case: October and early November weather hit seasonal demand, the F4Q Old Navy comp guide is -1% to -2%, and incremental promotion at Old Navy and Athleta lowered the FY26 gross margin outlook. GS calls Old Navy a show-me story and Athleta a significant offset.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Old Navy failing to return to positive and consistent comp trends with stronger merchandise margin delivery.

theme_stances.key_argument: GS is encouraged by Old Navy's sequential improvement but says further improvement is needed to drive stock outperformance.
theme_stances.evidence: remain constructive but acknowledge further improvement in Old Navy will be necessary
